ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a circle centered at B, with C above the circle, G below the circle, and segment CG passing vertically through B; A is at the lower left, D is at the upper right, and segment AD passes diagonally through B. The figure marks central angle ∠CBD as 55°. Reasoning: The problem states that AD and CG are both diameters of circle B, so B is the center of the circle, and BC, BD, and BG are all radii. The measure of the minor arc CD intercepted by central angle ∠CBD is equal to 55°. The required m\widehat{CGD} is the arc from C to D that passes through G, so it is the major arc CD. The whole circle is 360°, so m\widehat{CGD} = 360° - 55° = 305°.

raw_record.question_text: $\overline{AD}$ and $\overline{CG}$ are diameters of $\odot B$. Find $m\widehat{CGD}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: circle centered at B has C and G opposite on a vertical diameter, and A and D opposite on a slanted diameter. The image labels the central angle between radii BC and BD as 55°. From the text, AD and CG are diameters, so B is the center and BC, BD, BG are radii. The minor arc CD has measure equal to central angle CBD, so m arc CD = 55°. The requested arc CGD is the arc from C to D that passes through G, i.e. the major arc CD rather than the minor arc. Therefore m arc CGD = 360° - 55° = 305°.
